# ax-command

One definition of a command: its words, effect, arguments and flags, examples and output. From it come the parser (whose refusals name the exact fix), the usage and help, `help --json` and the MCP tool's input schema, so the CLI and the MCP server can never disagree.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/ax-command#v1.3.12
```

It installs `lib/ouro/ax/command.ts`, with `ax-effects`, `ax-exit-codes`, `ax-outcome`, `ax-problem`, `ax-voice`, `ax-wait`. Its tests are `ax-command-tests`. Every item runs on Node 22.18 or later as it is copied: the files import each other as `./<file>.ts`. The [Ouro AX guide](../guides/ax.md) shows how they fit together.

## Exports

### `AGENT_FLAG`

The flag a self-scoped command takes: who is calling. The kit compares it with the item's owner, so an agent acts on its own item only.

```ts
const AGENT_FLAG: FlagSpec
```

### `ArgSpec`

```ts
interface ArgSpec {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  required?: boolean;
  rest?: boolean | "list";
  stdin?: boolean;
  unless?: string | readonly string[];
  source?: string;
  missing?: string;
  values?: readonly string[];
}
```

### `argUsage`

`<name>`, `[<name>]` or `<name...>`, as usage shows an argument.

```ts
function argUsage(a: ArgSpec): string
```

### `BUILTIN_FLAGS`

```ts
const BUILTIN_FLAGS: Readonly<Record<string, FlagSpec>>
```

### `checkInput`

Checks an MCP call's arguments against the command, as the parser checks argv: an unknown property names the nearest, a wrong type or a missing value names it. The fix is the arguments to send instead, as JSON.

```ts
function checkInput(cli: Cli<RunContext>, cmd: CommandDef<unknown, RunContext>, raw: unknown, thing?: string): Readonly<Record<string, InputValue>>
```

### `checkOwner`

Refuses a self-scoped call on an item that is not the calling agent's (`not-yours`, the usage exit): it names whose item it is and who called, and gives the command for the caller's own item (`self.instead`) or says to ask the person. It passes a command without `self`, and the owner's own call. runCli, dispatch and the MCP server call it before plan() or run(); a tool that runs commands its own way calls it too.

```ts
function checkOwner<C extends RunContext>(cli: Cli<C>, cmd: CommandDef<unknown, C>, input: Readonly<Record<string, InputValue>>, ctx: C) => Promise<void>
```

### `Cli`

```ts
interface Cli<C extends RunContext = RunContext> {
  readonly name: string;

  readonly personOnly: Readonly<Record<string, PersonOnly>>;

  readonly outcomeExits: OutcomeExits;
  readonly waitExits: WaitExits;
  readonly voice: VoiceDef;
}
```

### `CliDef`

```ts
interface CliDef<C extends RunContext = RunContext> {
  name: string;
  about: readonly string[];
  commands: readonly CommandDef<unknown, C>[];
  exits?: ExitTable;
  headings?: EffectHeadings;
  globalFlags?: Readonly<Record<string, FlagSpec>>;
  ambiguous?: Readonly<Record<string, readonly Meaning[]>>;
  personOnly?: Readonly<Record<string, PersonOnly>>;
  groups?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  outcomeExits?: OutcomeExits;
  waitExits?: WaitExits;
  voice?: VoiceDef;
}
```

### `CommandDef`

A command's definition. `C` is the context run() and plan() get: RunContext, or an adopter's own that extends it.

```ts
interface CommandDef<R = unknown, C extends RunContext = RunContext> {
  name: string;
  aliases?: readonly string[];
  summary: string;
  effect: Effect;
  readOnly?: boolean;
  why?: "required" | "optional" | "none";
  args?: readonly ArgSpec[];
  flags?: Readonly<Record<string, FlagSpec>>;
  examples?: readonly string[];
  output?: string;
  hidden?: boolean;
  summarizes?: boolean;
  loose?: boolean;
  self?: SelfScope<C>;
  run?(input: Input, ctx: C): R | Promise<R>;
  plan?(input: Input, ctx: C): Outcome | Promise<Outcome>;
  text?(result: R, input: Input): string;
}
```

### `defineCli`

Builds the tool and checks its definitions: unique names, a valid exit table, examples that parse.

```ts
function defineCli<C extends RunContext = RunContext>(def: CliDef<C>) => Cli<C>
```

### `defineCommand`

```ts
function defineCommand<R, C extends RunContext = RunContext>(def: CommandDef<R, C>) => CommandDef<R, C>
```

### `exampleArgv`

An example's words after the tool's name, up to a pipe; null when the tool is not in it.

```ts
function exampleArgv(tool: string, example: string): string[] | null
```

### `findCommand`

The command the leading words name (the longest match), and how many words it took.

```ts
function findCommand(cli: Pick<Cli<RunContext>, "commands">, words: readonly string[]): { command: CommandDef<unknown, RunContext>; used: number; } | null
```

### `flagsOf`

The flags a command takes: the built-ins, the tool's, --why where asked for, --dry-run on an "others" command, then its own; a command's own flag replaces a generated one of the same name, except a self-scoped command's `--agent`, which the owner check needs.

```ts
function flagsOf(cli: Pick<Cli<RunContext>, "globalFlags">, cmd: CommandDef<unknown, RunContext>): Record<string, FlagSpec>
```

### `Meaning`

One meaning of an ambiguous word, and the command for it. `use` may hold `{args}`, the words the agent gave after the ambiguous word in that command's argument slots (a slot with none shows its placeholder), and `{flags}`, the flags the agent gave that the command takes (a sensitive value as its placeholder). A flag `use` writes out itself, such as `--why <why>`, gives way to the same flag given.

```ts
interface Meaning {
  means: string;
  use: string;
}
```

### `parse`

Parses argv against the definitions. Throws an AxError (exit "usage") whose fix is the corrected command line: an unknown flag names the nearest one, a missing argument shows where it goes and where to get it, a missing --why is appended, an ambiguous word lists each meaning's command.

```ts
function parse(cli: Cli<RunContext>, argv: readonly string[]): Parsed | HelpAsked
```

### `Parsed`

```ts
interface Parsed {
  kind: "run";
  command: CommandDef;
  input: Input;
  json: boolean;
  unchecked: Readonly<Record<string, string | true>>;
}
```

### `PersonOnly`

Words only the person acts on, such as `unmute`: the reason, one sentence to you, the agent ("You can't turn on the person's microphone; only they can."), and how the person does it (`with the microphone button in the call's controls`). The words refuse, `refused`, with both in one line, and `help --json` lists them under `personOnly`, so an agent learns them before it tries.

```ts
interface PersonOnly {
  reason: string;
  how: string;
}
```

### `RunContext`

```ts
interface RunContext {
  stdin(): Promise<string>;
  json: boolean;
}
```

### `SelfScope`

A command an agent may run only on its own item, such as its own row in the person's list of listening agents (the twin of a component action declared `scope: "self"`). The command takes `--agent <you>`, and the kit asks `owner` whose item the call names, before plan() or run(): when it is not the calling agent's, the call is refused (`not-yours`) and nothing runs. `help --json` marks the command `scope: "self"`.

```ts
interface SelfScope<C extends RunContext = RunContext> {
  owner(input: Input, ctx: C): string | null | Promise<string | null>;
  instead?: string;
}
```

### `toArgv`

The argv that runs a command with this input, the way an agent would type it; the first stdin-capable argument's text goes on stdin ("-"), so text that starts with "-" or spans lines passes whole.

```ts
function toArgv(cli: Pick<Cli<RunContext>, "globalFlags">, cmd: CommandDef<unknown, RunContext>, input: Readonly<Record<string, InputValue>>): { argv: string[]; stdin: string | null; }
```

### `usageOf`

The command's usage line from its definition: words, arguments, required flags, then the optional ones.

```ts
function usageOf(cli: Pick<Cli<RunContext>, "globalFlags">, cmd: CommandDef<unknown, RunContext>): string
```
